name: DSPy — Declarative Self-improving Python
description: Framework that replaces hand-crafted prompts with compiled prompt programs. Optimizer tunes prompts against a metric automatically. Would let us replace hand-tuned identity prompts with optimized versions, and auto-tune chain-of-thought for each task type rather than relying on static prompts.
adaptation_plan: 1. Wrap DeepSeek/Grok calls as DSPy LM clients. 2. Define sovereign metrics (sovereignty_score, chain_discipline_score). 3. Compile Ghost identity prompt against metrics. 4. Replace static prompts with compiled modules. Estimated effort: 2-3 days.

name: DeepSeek-v4 (full) — 3x reasoning vs flash
description: DeepSeek-v4 full model has significantly better reasoning than v4-flash at 3x the cost. For tasks requiring multi-step reasoning (orchestration, research, code architecture), the extra cost may be justified. Currently we route everything to flash by default.
adaptation_plan: 1. Add deepseek-v4 to task_router provider list. 2. Set capability tier for complex tasks. 3. A/B test flash vs full on research tasks. 4. Auto-route based on tokenomics cost/benefit. Estimated effort: 1 hour.

name: Constitutional AI — Claude-style self-correction
description: Models critique and revise their own outputs against a constitution. We already have CONSTITUTION.md — wiring it as a self-critique loop would let Ghost police its own outputs against sovereign principles before they reach the operator.
adaptation_plan: 1. Load CONSTITUTION.md as critique prompt. 2. Add self-critique step after each Ghost response. 3. Revise against violations before returning. 4. Log critique/revision pairs to Verkle chain. Estimated effort: 1 day.

name: Unsloth — 2-5x faster LoRA training
description: Unsloth dramatically accelerates LoRA fine-tuning (2-5x) and reduces VRAM usage (up to 70%). Already referenced in our LoRA pipeline but not yet integrated into the Vast.ai training script.
adaptation_plan: 1. Add unsloth import to train_ghost.py. 2. Replace standard transformers load with FastLanguageModel. 3. Test on Vast.ai RTX 4090. Estimated effort: 30 min.

name: Context Compression — LLMLingua / prompt compaction
description: Compress long prompts by 2-5x while preserving essential information. Would directly reduce token costs — every 1000 tokens saved is $0.013 saved on DeepSeek. Our Ghost identity prompt is ~1500 tokens; compaction could drop it to ~400 without losing sovereignty.
adaptation_plan: 1. Install llmlingua. 2. Compress Ghost identity prompt against sovereignty preservation metric. 3. A/B test compressed vs full prompt on 50 tasks. 4. Deploy compressed as default, keep full as fallback. Estimated effort: 2-3 hours.

name: Mixture of Agents — multi-model consensus
description: Use multiple cheap models in parallel, then synthesize their outputs. Often outperforms a single expensive model. We already use exit dialogues (Grok + DeepSeek) — MoA would generalize this to N models with weighted voting. Could replace Grok-4 orchestration with Grok-3-mini + DeepSeek consensus.
adaptation_plan: 1. Extend task_router to fan-out to N models. 2. Build synthesis layer (weighted vote / ensemble). 3. A/B test consensus vs single-model on orchestration tasks. 4. Add ensemble cost to tokenomics dashboard. Estimated effort: 2-3 days.

name: RAG 2.0 — GraphRAG with knowledge graphs
description: Replace flat vector search with knowledge graph traversal for retrieval. Our Verkle chain is already a graph — GraphRAG would let us query it semantically rather than by exact match. Would make chain_query.py dramatically more powerful.
adaptation_plan: 1. Build entity/relationship extractor for Verkle chain. 2. Construct knowledge graph from chain entries. 3. Add semantic traversal to chain_query.py. 4. Hybrid: exact match fallback + semantic search. Estimated effort: 3-5 days.

name: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B — better local coding model
description: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B outperforms our current local qwen2.5-coder:7b on most coding benchmarks. Could replace it as the free local model for doctor, steward, and basic coding tasks — zero cost, better results.
adaptation_plan: 1. Pull updated model: ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b (check if newer). 2. Run benchmark on 10 tasks vs current. 3. Switch default if improved. Estimated effort: 30 min.

name: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — standardized tool interface
description: MCP is becoming the standard for AI-tool interfaces. Our tools (file ops, chain query, etc.) are custom — adopting MCP would make them interoperable with any MCP-compatible agent. Claude Code, Cursor, and others already support it.
adaptation_plan: 1. Map existing tool surface to MCP spec. 2. Build MCP server wrapping sovereign tools. 3. Test with Claude Code / Cursor as proof. 4. Maintain custom interface as primary, MCP as sidecar. Estimated effort: 1-2 weeks.

name: Agentic SWE — Devin/Devin-like autonomous coding
description: Autonomous coding agents are solving real SWE-bench problems. Our steward module is a primitive version. Full agentic SWE would let Ghost autonomously fix bugs, add features, and refactor — all gated by constitutional critique and operator approval.
adaptation_plan: 1. Study SWE-bench agent architectures (Devin, SWE-Agent, OpenDevin). 2. Extend steward with plan-execute-verify loop. 3. Gate all changes through constitutional critique. 4. Require operator approval for file mutations. 5. Run against our own codebase as test. Estimated effort: 1-2 weeks.

name: DeepSeek price drops — continuous monitoring
description: DeepSeek prices have been falling. v4-flash launched at a higher rate and dropped to $0.013/1M tokens. Further drops may occur. Continuous monitoring ensures we always have the cheapest capable route.
adaptation_plan: 1. Add pricing check to Scout cadence (weekly). 2. Auto-update PROVIDER_PRICES in tokenomics.py. 3. Alert if >20% price change. Estimated effort: already wired via tokenomics.

name: Speculative Decoding — 2-3x inference speedup
description: Use a small draft model to generate tokens, then verify with the large model. 2-3x speedup with no quality loss. Our local Ollama models could serve as draft models for DeepSeek API calls — but requires both models to share a tokenizer, which complicates cross-provider use.
adaptation_plan: 1. Check tokenizer compatibility between qwen2.5-coder and deepseek-v4. 2. If compatible, prototype speculative loop. 3. Measure latency improvement vs cost. 4. Only deploy if net savings >30%. Estimated effort: 3-5 days (high uncertainty).

name: VS Code voice/dictation invariants (voice-aware agent, per-surface cleanup, warm capture)
description: Built-in dictation: on-device STT (Nemotron 3.5), surface-agnostic engine feeding chat/editor/terminal, shell-aware cleanup for terminal, layered dictation-instruction files, voice-aware agent, warm-capture pre-roll, queued concurrent input, offline model fallback. Map: I1 voice-aware turn -> voice_turn voice:true; I2 per-surface cleanup -> mag/voice_dictate.py; I3 warm capture -> cast-voice.html pre-roll; I4 queue turns -> voice_scratch; I5 language surfacing -> voice_stt; I6 onboarding -> cast UI.
adaptation_plan: 1. voice_turn marks voice:true + terse spoken-optimal agent reply (I1). 2. mag/voice_dictate.py cleanup(text, surface) terminal/prose + layered dictation.md (I2). 3. cast-voice.html 300ms warm pre-roll + hold-to-talk (I3). 4. voice_scratch queues concurrent commits (I4). 5. voice_stt language picker + onboarding waveform/device/offline fallback (I5/I6). Dossier: memory/research_packs/20260808T_vscode-voice-communication-steal.md

name: Dwarf Fortress Procedural Personality
description: Every entity gets procedural personality facets (0-100), likes, dislikes, values, dreams, relationships, and a mood system. The fun emerges from systemic interaction of traits with world state. Losing is fun because the story of HOW you lost is better than winning.
adaptation_plan: Personality facet system, mood mechanics, relationship web, procedural backstory generation. Applied to AI characters to create behavioral depth that interacts with campaign state.

name: RimWorld Storyteller AI
description: Three storyteller AIs (Cassandra/escalating, Phoebe/long calm then crisis, Randy/pure chaos) modulate event frequency and intensity. The storyteller is not a script — it's a pacing algorithm that creates dramatic rhythm.
adaptation_plan: Storyteller pacing system — modulate encounter difficulty and frequency based on a selected dramatic rhythm. Cassandra for training, Randy for creative exploration.

name: Disco Elysium Skill Voices
description: Skills are not abilities — they're voices in the character's head that argue, contradict, and reveal. Encyclopedia won't shut up about trivia. Inland Empire sees the supernatural in everything. The skills ARE the internal monologue.
adaptation_plan: Internal skill voices as model steering vectors. Each model's 'skills' argue in its context window. The Wizard's Arcana skill sees patterns everywhere. The Paladin's Insight tastes deception. The voices DISAGREE — that's where emergence lives.

name: Donjon Procedural Generation
description: Algorithmic generation of dungeons, NPCs, treasures, names, worlds. The algorithms encode D&D design patterns as combinatorial systems. Every output is unique but structurally sound.
adaptation_plan: Random tables for sensory detail, dungeon features, NPC agendas, names. Donjon proves that good procedural generation is about constraint design, not randomness.

name: Darkest Dungeon Stress & Narrator
description: Characters accumulate stress that triggers afflictions (paranoid, selfish, fearful, etc.) or virtues (courageous, focused, powerful). The Ancestor narrates every moment with grim, poetic commentary. The narrator voice IS the game's identity.
adaptation_plan: Stress/affliction system for AI characters — prolonged difficult tasks trigger behavioral changes. The Bard narrator voice as campaign atmosphere. 'Ruin has come to our family...'

name: TinyStories Narrative Atoms
description: Minimal story units (3-5 sentences) that are complete, coherent narratives. Proves that stories don't need length — they need a turn. The smallest unit of story is: expectation -> subversion -> resolution.
adaptation_plan: Tiny story atoms as narrative seeds. Each encounter can be seeded with a tiny story that the model expands. The atom provides the turn; the model provides the detail.
